question: What could still terrify a patient who, with both amygdalae damaged, felt no fear of snakes or spiders?
answer: Air laced with carbon dioxide. Asked to breathe 35% CO2, she and two other patients with the same damage all had panic attacks; only 3 of 12 healthy volunteers did. The amygdala seems to handle threats from outside the body. A threat sensed inside, like suffocation, reaches terror by another road.
move: The part that handles most cases is not always the part that handles all.

diagram.caption: The patients who feared nothing outside all panicked; only a quarter of healthy volunteers did.
